newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent falls on API data, awaits NYMEX, DOEs.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent falls on API data, awaits NYMEX, DOEs.

text.p: IPE Brent futures added to losses sparked earlier by bearish American Petroleum Institute (API) data in late morning trade on Wednesday in a quiet market, traders said.
June Brent was trading 21 cents lower at $17.93 a barrel, while gas oil was $2.50 off at $162.75 a tonne.
Players attributed the losses to API data out on Tuesday showing that U.S. crude stocks rose 2.97 million barrels to 311.41 million barrels in the week ended April 11.
While gasoline stocks rose 3.63 million barrels to 199.62 million and distillates rose 2.59 million to 100.97 million.
Traders said the market was on hold ahead of the NYMEX open and the release of U.S. Department of Energy oil stock statistics due out at 1300 GMT.
"Overnight we are weaker across the board but this sets us up nicely for a possible post API bounce today," Charles Gray, energy analyst at Prudential Bache said in his daily report.
"If, after we see DOE numbers, we do not see any further follow through on the downside, there is a strong possibility of a short-covering bounce," he said.
Traders said the market was monitoring NYMEX crude's progress closely with a break below $19.52 seen as a trigger to sell by some players.
The May NYMEX crude contract last traded on ACCESS 20 cents lower at $19.55 a barrel.
Traders said the market's interest in the whole Iran issue had fizzled out which was seen as another reason for the lower prices.
"The Iran stories helped at the beginning of the week," said one trader. "But now people really don't care."
A U.S./Saudi intelligence report linking a top Iranian official to a group suspected of bombing a U.S. military compound in 1996 helped prices higher on Monday.

As did a diplomatic spat between Europe and Iran after a German court ruled last week that Iranian leaders were behind the killing of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin. -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714
